# `hs-run security` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run security` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `leak_found` | A secret is exposed in this tree — a tracked `.env` file, a matched credential pattern, or both. Remove it from the commit and ROTATE the credential before anything else; a deleted file whose key still works is not a fix. | `references/secret-and-dependency.md`, `references/secret-lifecycle-7stage.md` |
| `scan_incomplete` | Part of this tree was never read — an untracked nested repository the scan cannot descend into, or a file it lacks permission to open. Not a finding and not a clean result: check the listed paths yourself before concluding anything about the rest. | `counting-discipline`, `references/scan-dimensions.md` |
| `no_repo` | There is no git repository here, so every git-based read was SKIPPED. Zero findings means zero reads, not zero secrets — scan the whole tree by hand, or re-run from inside the repository that owns these files. | `counting-discipline`, `references/secret-and-dependency.md` |
| `env_unprotected` | Nothing has leaked, but an untracked `.env` is on disk and the ignore rules do not cover it — one careless `git add .` away from the state above. The envelope carries the one command that closes it. | `references/secret-lifecycle-7stage.md` |
| `swept_clear` | The mechanical sweep finished and found nothing on the surface it reads. That surface is NARROW — this is the start of the security pass, not the end. Run the STRIDE/OWASP reasoning, using the dependency-audit command the envelope names. | `verification-mechanism`, `orchestration-protocol`, `references/threat-model.md`, `references/scan-dimensions.md`, `references/dependency-risk-deep.md` |
| `swept_clear_no_dep_tool` | Same clear sweep, and this stack declares NO dependency-audit command. Say that out loud in the report rather than naming a runner that does not exist here. | `verification-mechanism`, `references/threat-model.md`, `references/scan-dimensions.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `repo_unreadable` | git itself could not answer, so nothing in this tree was measured. Repair the repository first; a clear result from a broken probe is worth nothing. |
